title: The Great Gatsby — Opening Arrival
adaptation_scope: From Nick’s recalled advice from his father through his settling at West Egg and first sight of Gatsby’s mansion (Chapter 1 opening excerpt).

style_bible.visual_period: United States, 1915–1922: Middle West to Long Island, summer 1922
style_bible.line_and_color: Clean, precise ink lines with restrained color; sandy neutrals and cool bay blues punctuated by warm golds and ivy greens; occasional double-exposure overlays for metaphor.
style_bible.lighting: Golden hour exteriors; crisp summer sunlight; lamplit interiors with soft shadows; dusk blues over the bay.
style_bible.lettering: Narration captions in elegant serif italics; dialogue in clean uppercase sans; sound effects small and unobtrusive.
recurring_motifs: Water of Long Island Sound shimmering at dusk

characters.name: Nick Carraway
characters.visual_anchor: Slim, clean-shaven man in his mid-20s; neatly parted brown hair; observant gray-blue eyes; reserved posture.
characters.costume: 1922 light wool suit (tan or gray), white shirt, slim tie, straw boater or flat cap as needed; in college/war flashbacks: Yale sweater or WWI doughboy uniform.
characters.expression_range: Subtle: thoughtful, politely attentive, faintly amused, quietly weary.
characters.continuity_note: Keep Nick’s hair part, lean build, and understated dress consistent; he often stands slightly apart from others, hands in pockets or holding a notebook/book.

characters.name: Nick’s Father
characters.visual_anchor: Older gentleman with neat silver-streaked hair and small mustache; calm, direct gaze.
characters.costume: Dark three-piece suit with pocket watch chain; white shirt; conservative tie.
characters.continuity_note: Appears only in memory; keep porch setting and twilight tone consistent.

characters.name: Confiding Young Men (composite)
characters.visual_anchor: Assorted college-age men with loosened ties or varsity sweaters; slightly haggard or intense looks.
characters.costume: 1910s collegiate attire: shirtsleeves, vests, lettered sweaters.
characters.continuity_note: Use as background foils; avoid distinct anchors so they read as various ‘wild, unknown men.’

characters.name: Finnish Housekeeper
characters.visual_anchor: Sturdy middle-aged woman with kerchief over hair and kind, lined face; practical stance.
characters.costume: Simple long skirt, rolled sleeves, apron; sensible shoes.
characters.expression_range: Stoic, murmuring concentration; occasional curt nod.
characters.continuity_note: Always near the stove or housekeeping tasks; include small muttered SFX rather than dialogue.

characters.name: Direction-Seeking Man
characters.visual_anchor: Newly arrived young man with soft hat and travel-creased suit; earnest, a bit lost.
characters.costume: Light summer suit with loosened tie; scuffed shoes; carrying a folded timetable.
characters.continuity_note: Appears only once on the country road; keep him hat-in-hand when he asks.

characters.name: Jay Gatsby (distant presence)
characters.visual_anchor: Handsome man mid-30s seen in silhouette or at a distance; straight posture; slicked dark hair.
characters.costume: Evening wear or immaculate light suit depending on scene; no close facial detail yet.
characters.continuity_note: Show him as a silhouette/figure on terrace or near water; withhold close facial features until later chapters.

pages.page_summary: Nick recalls his father’s advice and his habit of reserving judgment, with glimpses of college confidences and the limits of his tolerance.

panels.image_prompt: 1910s Middle Western front porch at twilight; Nick as a teenager sits beside his father on wooden chairs; father leans forward, hand gently raised, giving counsel. Fireflies hover; a quiet street and elm trees in soft purple dusk. Period suits: father in dark three-piece, young Nick in simple shirt and suspenders. Warm lamplight from inside spills onto the porch.
panels.caption: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me advice.

dialogue.speaker: Father
dialogue.text: Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone, remember not everyone had your advantages.

panels.continuity_notes: Establish young Nick’s look for later recognition; father’s measured tone.
panels.source_anchor: "Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone... advantages that you've had."

panels.beat: Nick’s habit of reserving judgments opens confidences—and bores.
panels.image_prompt: 1910s college dorm common room at night; Nick, older now, sits on a threadbare couch, posture attentive but reserved; a disheveled student leans in, whispering intensely. Books and empty coffee cups litter a table; a green-shaded desk lamp casts moody pools of light.
panels.caption: So I reserve all judgments. It opens curious natures to me—and not a few veteran bores.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep Nick’s calm listening pose; composite confider can vary later.
panels.source_anchor: "I'm inclined to reserve all judgements... victim of not a few veteran bores."

panels.beat: Feigning sleep to avoid another ‘intimate revelation.’
panels.image_prompt: Dormitory bunk room; late night. Nick lies on a narrow bed, eyes closed, one arm over his face, coat hanging on a hook. Another student stands in the doorway, hesitant, about to speak. A single bare bulb glows.
panels.caption: Often I feigned sleep when an intimate revelation quivered on the horizon.
panels.source_anchor: "Frequently I have feigned sleep... an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon."

panels.beat: Accused in college of being a ‘politician’ for knowing secret griefs.
panels.image_prompt: College quad by day; Nick walks past bulletin boards while two students whisper and glance his way. Autumn leaves on the ground; a stone building backdrop.
panels.caption: The abnormal mind attaches to this quality. They called me a politician—privy to secret griefs.
panels.continuity_notes: Campus setting contrasts with prior interiors.
panels.source_anchor: "I was unjustly accused of being a politician... privy to the secret griefs of wild, unknown men."

panels.beat: Limits of tolerance; decencies unequally parceled.
panels.image_prompt: City sidewalk afternoon; Nick stands still, hands in pockets, as passersby of different classes stream past: a banker in a topcoat, a laborer with lunch pail, a flapper with beads. Long shadow lines; muted colors.
panels.caption: Decencies are parceled unequally at birth. Even tolerance has a limit.
panels.continuity_notes: Externalize internal thought via contrasting passersby; keep Nick centered, slightly apart.
panels.source_anchor: "a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally... I come to the admission that it has a limit."

pages.page_summary: Nick’s post-Eastern reaction, his singular exception for Gatsby, the ‘foul dust,’ and his background leading to the move East.

panels.beat: After returning last autumn, Nick longs for a world at moral attention.
panels.image_prompt: City street in late autumn; a line of uniformed men (soldiers, police) stand at attention along a curb; Nick in civilian suit passes by, posture rigid, eyes forward. Pale sunlight; bare trees.
panels.caption: After I came back from the East, I wanted the world in uniform—at moral attention.
panels.continuity_notes: Temporal cue: ‘last autumn’; cooler palette than summer scenes.
panels.source_anchor: "I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever."

panels.beat: Only Gatsby is exempt; he both offends and fascinates.
panels.image_prompt: Night on Long Island Sound; distant silhouette of a man (Gatsby) on a terrace above dark lawns, looking across the bay; soft party lights behind him; the water glimmers.
panels.caption: Only Gatsby was exempt—he represented what I scorn, yet there was something gorgeous about him.
panels.continuity_notes: Do not reveal Gatsby’s face; emphasize distance and allure.
panels.source_anchor: "Only Gatsby... was exempt... there was something gorgeous about him."

panels.beat: Gatsby’s sensitivity like a machine registering distant earthquakes.
panels.image_prompt: Close on an early 20th-century seismograph: brass arm tapping a moving paper ribbon. Double-exposure overlay: faint profile of Gatsby’s silhouette aligned with the needle’s tremor.
panels.caption: A heightened sensitivity—an extraordinary gift for hope.
panels.continuity_notes: Introduce the seismograph motif for reuse; keep overlay subtle.
panels.source_anchor: "as if he were related to one of those intricate machines that register earthquakes... an extraordinary gift for hope."

panels.beat: ‘Foul dust’ in the wake of Gatsby’s dreams.
panels.image_prompt: Dusk over the bay; a small motorboat’s wake ripples toward shore; in the air above the water, dust-like motes swirl in the last light, mingled with stray confetti.
panels.caption: He turned out all right. It was the foul dust in the wake of his dreams that closed my interest in short-winded elations.
panels.continuity_notes: Set up ‘dust’ as a recurring visual; keep colors somber blue-violets.
panels.source_anchor: "what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams... closed out my interest..."

panels.beat: Background: Middle West, Yale, the war; restlessness and decision to go East.
panels.image_prompt: Triptych montage: 1) Formal family portrait in a Middle Western parlor; 2) Yale 1915 diploma with mortarboard on a table; 3) Nick in WWI uniform crouched in a trench; 4) Seamless into a spring 1922 train roaring east past green fields.
panels.caption: Prominent Middle West. Yale ’15. The war. Restless—I went East to learn the bond business.
panels.continuity_notes: Anchor dates subtly (1915, spring ’22) via props; keep Nick identifiable across vignettes.
panels.source_anchor: "My family have been prominent... Yale in 1915... the Great War... so I decided to go East and learn the bond business."

pages.page_summary: Nick’s West Egg setup: the bungalow, Finnish housekeeper, brief dog, first neighborly exchange, summer’s fresh start, and the Eggs—culminating in Gatsby’s colossal mansion beside Nick’s small house.

panels.beat: The weather-beaten bungalow at eighty a month; roommate sent to Washington.
panels.image_prompt: Morning in a quiet coastal commuting town; a small weathered shingle bungalow with a sagging porch near the water; wild grass; a paper tacked inside the window (rent $80/month). Nick arrives with a suitcase; a second suitcase sits abandoned on the porch with a telegram atop: ‘Ordered to Washington.’
panels.caption: A weather-beaten cardboard bungalow at eighty a month. My would-be roommate went to Washington; I went alone.
panels.continuity_notes: Place the house near visible water to foreshadow proximity to the Sound.
panels.source_anchor: "a weather-beaten cardboard bungalow at eighty a month... the firm ordered him to Washington, and I went out... alone."

panels.beat: A few-day dog, old Dodge, and the Finnish woman at the electric stove.
panels.image_prompt: Cozy kitchen interior; morning sun; the Finnish housekeeper stirs a pan on an electric stove, muttering. Nick sits at a small table with coffee; on a wall hook hangs an empty dog leash and collar. Through a window, an old Dodge car is parked in a sandy drive.
panels.caption: I had a dog—for a few days—an old Dodge, and a Finnish woman who cooked and murmured wisdom to herself over the electric stove.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep the Dodge’s silhouette consistent in later exterior shots.
panels.source_anchor: "I had a dog—at least I had him for a few days... and a Finnish woman... muttered... over the electric stove."

panels.beat: A newer arrival asks Nick the way to West Egg village.
panels.image_prompt: Sunny country road lined with hedges and new leaves; the Direction-Seeking Man, hat in hand, looks helpless; Nick gestures down the road, relaxed now. A glimpse of bay water at the turn ahead.
panels.caption: Lonely, until a man newer than I stopped me on the road.

dialogue.speaker: Stranger
dialogue.text: How do you get to West Egg village?

dialogue.speaker: Nick
dialogue.text: Straight on, then left by the Sound.

panels.continuity_notes: Establish neighborly tone; same road returns visually in later Long Island sequences.
panels.source_anchor: "'How do you get to West Egg village?' he asked helplessly."

panels.beat: Summer’s restart; red-and-gold books like new money.
panels.image_prompt: Interior shelf close-up: a neat row of a dozen red-and-gold spined volumes titled ‘Banking,’ ‘Credit,’ ‘Investment Securities’; sunbeams cut dust in the air; faint reflection of bay light. Inset: Nick at a single window, reading.
panels.caption: With sunshine and bursting leaves, life began over again. I bought red-and-gold books—like new money from the mint.
panels.continuity_notes: Introduce the ‘single window’ reading posture as Nick’s POV motif.
panels.source_anchor: "bursts of leaves... life was beginning over again... I bought a dozen volumes... in red and gold like new money from the mint."

panels.beat: The two Eggs and Gatsby’s colossal mansion beside Nick’s tiny house.
panels.image_prompt: Aerial-like view of two egg-shaped peninsulas jutting into Long Island Sound under bright summer light; LEFT labeled ‘West Egg’ (less fashionable), RIGHT labeled ‘East Egg.’ Foreground lower strip: Nick’s small shingled house perched at the tip of West Egg, fifty yards from the water, squeezed between two vast estates. On the right estate: a spanking-new stone mansion imitating a Normandy town hall, with a single tower, raw ivy just starting, a marble swimming pool glinting, and sweeping lawns across forty acres.
panels.caption: That riotous island of two enormous Eggs. I lived at West Egg—my small house pinched between vast places. To my right stood a colossal imitation of a Normandy Hôtel de Ville—Gatsby’s mansion.
panels.continuity_notes: Keep mansion features consistent: tower, raw ivy, marble pool, vast lawn; do not show Gatsby up close.
panels.source_anchor: "two unusual formations... a pair of enormous eggs... I lived at West Egg... My house... squeezed between two huge places... a factual imitation of some Hôtel de Ville in Normandy... It was Gatsby's mansion."

open_questions: Do you want Gatsby’s distant figure to appear again in an early silent cameo on the mansion terrace, or preserve complete absence until the party chapter?
Should Nick’s Yale/war montage recur as brief flash inserts when he weighs judgments later, reinforcing his ‘single window’ motif?
Do you prefer labeled map-style captions for West vs. East Egg on the aerial panel, or diegetic signage within the environment?
